messages:
Maria Gomez: Morning handoff — I'm oncall until 9am PT tomorrow. Quick notes on routing/thresholds before I sign off.
Maria Gomez: TL;DR: lowered noisy-llm-timeout to 30s, suppressed low-priority batch-failure alerts 04:00-06:00 PT, and added a temporary route for eu-burst to eu-backup.
Maria Gomez: Details below, ping me if anything odd. Leaving monitoring watchlist: small-tail-latency, kv-cache-miss-rate.
Aditya Rao: Thanks — do you have the exact PD escalation policy you changed?
Maria Gomez: Yep — changed policy action for noisy-llm-timeout: was page -> now email+wait 2m -> page only if persists. Policy id: pd_policy:proj-llm-qos-97.
Aditya Rao: Nice. Will that impact our SLOs for interactive endpoints?
Maria Gomez: Minimal — this only gates pages for transient spikes. We still record incidents for SLO RB. If sustained beyond 2m it pages like before.
Kevin Li: Where did you add the eu-burst route? I want to update the router config in case we need to rollback.
Maria Gomez: Added routing rule in infra-routing repo -> path: services/llm/routing/eu.json line ~112, rule name 'eu-burst-temporary'. It pins to eu-backup (g4dn) and has a max qps of 120.
Kevin Li: Can you paste the rule snippet?
Maria Gomez: ```json
{"name": "eu-burst-temporary", "match": {"region":"eu","tag":"burst"}, "targets": ["eu-backup"], "max_qps": 120, "fallback": "eu-primary"}
```
Jesse Tran: Quick FYI — I ran a smoke eval on eu-backup last night, 95th latency was ~220ms under 50 concurrent. Should be fine for short bursts.
Aditya Rao: Re: suppressed batch-failure alerts 04:00-06:00 PT — is that only for the batch queue or global?
Maria Gomez: Only batch-queue:alert/batch-failure. Reason: nightly shard rebalances cause a lot of noise. I left a note in PagerDuty schedule: reason + rollback instructions.
oncall-bot: [automation] Applied maintenance window on service: batch-queue:alert/batch-failure from 2024-06-05T04:00-06:00 PT. Change-id: mw-20240605-33.
Kevin Li: Thanks. I'll add a quick dashboard panel showing suppressed alert counts so we can ensure nothing important is lost.
Jesse Tran: Heads-up — a minor config caveat: the eu routing entry doesn't include the new kv-cache hotfix tag. If traffic is routed there without the hotfix, we might see higher cache misses.
Maria Gomez: Good catch. I intentionally left that out because the hotfix causes a memory regrowth on g4dn in some cases. Plan: keep hotfix off eu-backup for now, monitor kv-cache-miss-rate, and if it spikes, we'll divert back to eu-primary.
Aditya Rao: How will we trigger the diversion? Manual?
Maria Gomez: For now manual — Kevin or I can flip the rule in infra-routing and redeploy. I left a step-by-step in the handoff playbook: /playbooks/oncall/routing-divert.md with commands. Example: `curl -X POST https://infra-api/redeploy -d '{"rule":"eu-burst-temporary","action":"disable"}'`
Kevin Li: Copy. I'll check permissions for that API key before you go.
Jesse Tran: One more: I noticed an uptick in noisy-llm-timeout count this morning, likely a client-side marshalling bug. Filing an issue and tagging sdk-team.
Jesse Tran: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 — added reproduction steps.
Aditya Rao: Cool. If pages start coming through, I'll escalate per pd_policy:proj-llm-qos-97.
Maria Gomez: Thanks all. Off to a meeting — leaving pager with Aditya. If anything critical, DM me. :wave:
oncall-bot: Maria Gomez removed from oncall rotation at 2024-06-04T16:20:00Z. Aditya Rao is now primary.
Aditya Rao: I'm on. Scanning graphs and dashboards now.
Kevin Li: Adding the suppressed-alerts panel to the main oncall dashboard — ETA 20m.
Jesse Tran: I'll keep an eye on kv-cache-miss-rate and post if it crosses 4%.
Aditya Rao: Thanks team.
Maria Gomez: (closing note) keep an eye on the 95th for interactive endpoints during eu bursts. If sustained >350ms for more than 5m, switch route back and page SRE.
